[[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] used '''specific code cylinders''' to provide its [[Officer/Legends|officers]] with security clearance codes. In combination with the [[Rank insignia plaque/Legends|rank plaques]], these [[Code cylinder/Legends|code cylinders]] could also be used to denote rank within the hierarchy. Imperial code cylinders were introduced since the early [[Standard day/Legends|days]] of the new regime, and they remained in use among the Imperial splinter factions after the Empire collapsed at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]].

==Overview==
Imperial [[Code cylinder/Legends|code cylinders]] were among the most common access tools employed by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Standing regulations demanded that every [[Imperial officer/Legends|Imperial officer's]] code cylinders were in view at all time, and they were kept in narrow pockets on either side of the upper chest. However, only high ranking officers displayed them on their jacket; Imperial engineers and technicians wore them in special pockets around their neck or on their belt.<ref name="FF121">{{FactFile|121|IMP 1-2|Imperial Code Cylinders}}</ref>

Imperial installations were divided into a variety of sectors, each separated from others by security checkpoints. At major checkpoints, [[Officer/Legends|officers]] who wished to access the next secured area had to prove their identity and rank by inserting individualized cylinders into a [[Scomp link/Legends|scomp link]]. The scomp link interfaced with a centralized [[Computer/Legends|computer]], which determined whether the officer had the proper clearance before denying or approving their access request.<ref name="BTM" /> Due to their use, Imperial code cylinders enforced discipline among the lower ranks and contributed to the insignia of officers and subofficers by indicating seniority.<ref name="FF121" />

All officers of the Navy and Army were issued with at least one cylinder, which they were ordered to display at all time. A second device was sometimes issued when an officer's duty spanned a number of unrelated sectors. Admirals of the Fleet were usually issued with three code cylinders, which enabled them to access the intelligence databanks carried by capital ships.<ref name="FF121" /> Because each cylinder permitted access to only specific sectors, high-ranking officers carried up to four of them. Aboard the [[first]] [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]], [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]] possessed four cylinders, which allowed him to travel freely throughout the [[Moon/Legends|moon]]-sized battle station. In contrast, [[General/Legends|General]] [[Cassio Tagge/Legends|Cassio Tagge]] and [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Conan Antonio Motti/Legends|Conan Antonio Motti]] carried only three code cylinders.<ref name="BTM" />

While some officers considered the cylinders a mere mark of their status, the devices were also programmed to give the Empire a detailed knowledge of its servicemen's actions. The Imperial computer network kept detailed records of every cylinder's activity, including every time a sensitive file was accessed or a high-security area was entered. Such logs were monitored by agents of the [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]] who scanned the records in search of suspicious behavior&mdash;including over-frequent access to a secured file or area.<ref name="FF121" />

==Characteristics==
[[File:Alternate_code_cylinders.jpg|thumb|left|Imperial code cylinders came in a variety of shapes.]]
The Imperial code cylinders came in at least three different shapes, as the ones worn by Grand Moff Tarkin, Admiral Motti and the [[Stormtrooper/Legends|Stormtrooper]] officers were significantly distinct. The most common type of cylinders looked like thin pens with a small pocket clip and a blue tip containing the series code. Those worn by the Stormtrooper corps were shorter, with a different pocket clip. Admiral Motti's cylinder were thicker and featured a spiral drill bulb at the top,<ref name="SWVD">''[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> which was in fact the computer link itself.<ref name="FF121" />

==History==
The Galactic Empire used code cylinders from its early days on. When the [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] gathered most influential officers in order to introduce them to his new second-in-command, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], all of them already wore at least one code cylinder.<ref name="SWR78">[[Republic 78|''Republic'' 78]]</ref>

After the Empire collapsed at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], code cylinders remained in use in surviving Imperial outposts. The [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], the democratic government established by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]], also started to use similar coded cards or pass-keys to verify an individual's identity.<ref name="FF121" />

==Behind the scenes==
The code cylinders used by the Galactic Empire first appeared in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], the first installment of the ''Star Wars'' [[original trilogy]].<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> In the movies, some of the Imperial code cylinders were small pen-like radiation [[Wikipedia:Dosimeter|dosimeters]].<ref name="Set Piece">{{InsiderCite|96|Set Piece|Set Piece: Death Star Conference Room}}</ref> However, the Stormtrooper cylinders that were shown in ''[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]'' were in fact chalk holders that were provided to [[David West Reynolds]] by Mathew Clayson.<ref name="SWTC">{{WebCite|url=http://www.theforce.net/swtc/insignia/cylinders.html|text=Star Wars Technical Commentaries&mdash;Rank Cylinders|archivedate=20011108052501}}</ref>
